doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Germany instead of Korea
summary: Ali's mother felt she had risked him in Korea, but he served in Germany and learned drumming in the drum corps.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did you have any thoughts you might be sent over to Korea?

Yeah. You know that was the only mistake that my mom felt that she had made is to get me in harm’s way, because she insisted I go into the service because I was getting pretty stupid in the street. I had quit school, I didn’t want to go to school, I didn’t want to do anything other than hang out in the street, right? And so she put me in the Army and she really saved my life because I didn’t go to Korea, I went to Europe instead. And it was a blessing. But I had friends that went to Korea, and I had a couple of them that got hurt over there and everything, but I went to Germany. And I spent my last 2-1/2 years in Germany in the service. So I didn’t see anything like that. And I was in the Second Army Band so I had a real good, prosperous and a really good time in the Army. I learned a lot. I learned a lot about music and a lot about life.
I bet you learned how to roll, huh?
Yeah, I learned how to play the drums for real I learned how to play the drums, because I was in the drum corps, of course.
